lexicon: POINT-CONTACT — two bounded regions meet at exactly one point
description: A lemniscate: one closed run crossing itself once. Under CROSSING-IS-AN-EMERGENT-VERTEX the crossing is a degree-4 vertex, so the figure is ONE connected map with two bounded regions (the lobes) and one unbounded one. The two lobes share that single vertex and no edge. That is the structural content: boundaries meeting at a point, which is a weaker contact than corpus 007's ADJACENCY, where two regions share a whole edge. Derived, not assigned — the lobes do meet there, and the vertex is read off the ink rather than declared.
teaches: Module S: point-contact as a third RCC-8-adjacent relation — weaker than 007's edge-contact (EC) and stronger than 012's disconnection (DC). The lobes are distinguished from two separate circles by every vertex-side invariant — vertex count, components and degree sequence — and by no face relation.
provenance: Cosmic Codex orbit 13, reflect_pair(Wave), attested meaning 'infinity (SymbolFolds)'. The ATTESTED LABEL is not derived here and stays conventional; what is derived is the structural relation the figure instantiates. Note 071. The planar rotation was found by this repo's own tooling rejecting the interleaved order as genus 1 — a torus, not a page.
